hook: I built a hotel bed for $115. Here's proof.

scenes.visual_prompt: Before shot: flat, mismatched bed with worn comforter
scenes.voiceover: This is where I started — a comforter that had been through way too many wash cycles.

scenes.visual_prompt: Five items laid out on the bed before assembly: insert, cover, shams, accent pillows, fleece throw
scenes.voiceover: Five items, stacked, came out to $115.21 — comforter insert, duvet cover, shams, accent pillows, and a fleece throw.

scenes.visual_prompt: Grey fleece throw being folded in thirds across the foot of the bed
scenes.voiceover: The fleece throw alone has 179,574 ratings. It's one of the highest-reviewed bedding items on Amazon, period.

scenes.visual_prompt: Time-lapse of bed being layered: insert into cover, shams placed, accent pillows added, throw folded at foot
scenes.voiceover: Insert inside the cover first, then shams behind the sleeping pillows, then accent pillows, then the throw last.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final reveal: fully styled, plush, hotel-look bed with warm lighting
scenes.voiceover: This is the after. Not a $200 hotel duvet. $115.21 in five pieces.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card listing all 5 items with individual prices
scenes.voiceover: I broke down exactly what each piece costs and what the reviews actually say about it.

scenes.visual_prompt: CTA frame with blog post preview
scenes.voiceover: Every price, every review count, on the blog. Link's in my bio.

caption: $115.21. Five items. No $200 hotel duvet required. I priced out every single piece of this bed — comforter insert, duvet cover, shams, accent pillows, fleece throw — and checked what actual reviewers say about each one before I bought anything. Full breakdown on the blog, link in bio.
